relations.subject: clusters:disk-type
relations.evidence: AWS Choose between GP3 or IO2. GP3 disks are general-purpose and provide the best balance of price and performance, for provisioning performance and storage capacity independently. IO2 disks have higher performance, more durability, and better reliability.

relations.subject: clusters:disk-type
relations.evidence: GCP PD-SSD only - best for higher performance with lower latency and more IOPS.

relations.subject: clusters:disk-type
relations.evidence: Azure Choose between Premium SSD or Ultra disks. Premium SSDs are best for higher performance with lower latency and more IOPS. Ultra Disks are best for intensive, transaction-heavy workloads with low latency and consistent IOPS.

relations.subject: clusters:storage-auto-expansion
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - additional evidence for the already-promoted relation, this time from the cluster-configuration reference page rather than a Health Advisor mention
relations.evidence: For Multi-Node or Custom clusters deployed on Azure, Auto-Scaling is turned off by default, as it requires replacing and rebalancing nodes. This results in data movement and can affect performance until Auto-Scaling completes. You can choose whether to turn on Auto-Scale, or leave it turned off.

relations.subject: clusters:storage-auto-expansion
relations.evidence: For Multi-Node or Custom clusters deployed on AWS or GCP, automatic storage scaling is always on. You cannot turn off Auto-Scaling.

relations.subject: clusters:availability-zone
relations.evidence: Clusters on the **Basic** [Support Plan](#plan) support only a **Single** Availability Zone.

notable_absence.finding: The 'Cluster Configuration Options' bulleted list (the page's own enumeration of everything configurable when creating a paid cluster: name/description, basic cluster option, CSP/region, CIDR block, public-access restriction, Server version, services/service groups, nodes, compute, storage, support plan, availability zones) does NOT include storage engine. Storage engine/backend (Couchstore vs Magma) appears exactly once on this page, buried inside the Guardrails threshold table as part of two metric names ('Data Service Resident Ratio (Couchstore)' / '(Magma)'), with no explanation of where or when a user chooses one. This confirms this batch's hypothesis in the negative direction: reading the authoritative cluster-configuration page does NOT confirm storage-engine as a cluster-creation-time choice - if anything it suggests the opposite, that storage engine is set elsewhere (most likely per-bucket, out of this batch's scope).

cross_component_finding: Known recurring anomaly (server-version-string citation) recurs here: 'The latest supported version of Couchbase Server for Capella operational clusters is 8.0.' - a hardcoded version string of exactly the kind flagged in prior rounds as a staleness risk, not a new finding.
